subject: Ledgerly model-fit: recommended variants, acceptance gates, next steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Cheng <alex.cheng@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ledgerly model-fit: recommended variants, acceptance gates, next steps

Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a pragmatic path to decide whether an open-model stack can match your proprietary baseline for the Refund & Dispute triage workflow. I pulled together concrete recommendations so we can move to a short evaluation sprint.

Summary of what we heard on the call
- Primary goal: match or exceed current triage precision (proprietary baseline 'AcmeGen v3') while cutting inference cost ~30%.
- Key acceptance criteria you mentioned: top intent classification accuracy >= 92% on your labeled set; average latency < 350ms 95th pct under your traffic profile; visible reduction in hallucination for account-number extraction tasks.
- Constraint: data residency for PII — will run PoC in Redwood Dedicated in us-west.

Redwood recommended variants (prioritized for fast eval)
1) open-medium: Llama-2-13B-quant (8-bit quantized, Redwood-optimized kernels) — lowest latency, good token understanding for slot extraction.
2) open-large: Llama-2-70B-ggml-quant (KV cache enabled) — better few-shot robustness on ambiguous phrases, moderate cost.
3) baseline comparison: AcmeGen v3 (your in-house/proprietary baseline) — we'll treat as control.

Early benchmark plan (what we'll run in week-0 to week-2)
- Dataset: ledgerly_prod_sample_v1 (1k manually labeled examples you approved during call).
- Tests: intent accuracy, slot-extraction F1, hallucination rate (PII false positives), end-to-end latency distribution (95/99), safety scans for policy triggers.
- Acceptance gates: intent >= 92%, slot F1 within 5% of AcmeGen, hallucination rate <= current baseline, latency 95th <= 350ms on Dedicated.

Attachments I will drop into the shared folder: ledgerly_prompt_set_v1.json (prompt bundles + few-shot examples), and an initial A/B test plan (redwood_a_b_test_plan.pdf). Also linking a small bench I ran locally comparing tokenization edge cases: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-LLLedgerlyEval

Next steps (please confirm):
- You to share the 1k labeled sample and a sanitized example of the AcmeGen outputs by EOD Fri.
- We spin up a Dedicated PoC (2 weeks) with both open-medium and open-large variants and run the benchmark. Estimated cost for the eval is in the HubSpot quote I attached to the deal.
- If open variant passes acceptance gates, we propose a canary on a subset (5-10%) of live traffic for 4 weeks, then scale.

If this looks good I’ll schedule kickoff Monday.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
pri yom.das@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment stubs: ledgerly_prompt_set_v1.json (prompt bundle), redwood_a_b_test_plan.pdf (A/B plan)

From: Alex Cheng <alex.cheng@ledgerly.com>

Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ledgerly model-fit: recommended variants, acceptance gates, next steps

Priyom — this is great, thank you. A couple of clarifications from our side: 
1) The 92% threshold is for intent classification only; for slot-extraction (account numbers / amounts) we need F1 >= 0.88.
2) We can provide the 1k labeled sample but need to redact customer names and raw account numbers (we'll hash numeric strings — acceptable?).

We can get you the dataset by Friday. Regarding the AcmeGen exports: procurement needs an internal review before sharing detailed model outputs; can we start the eval using our labeled set first and then, if results look promising, provide anonymized AcmeGen outputs?

Also, curious about two practical items:
- Is the Dedicated PoC sufficient to reproduce your reported latency numbers, or do you need a mock of our routing layer?
- For the open-70B variant, can we expect any notable drop in slot extraction correctness due to quantization?

I'll confirm internal timelines and loop procurement.

— Alex
Alex Cheng
Head of ML | Ledgerly
alex.cheng@ledgerly.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ledgerly model-fit: recommended variants, acceptance gates, next steps

Thanks, Priyom and Alex — quick technical notes from my side on the quantization/parity risks and an actionable eval checklist we should run during the PoC.

A. Quantization impact (short):
- Llama-2-13B 8-bit quant: in our internal tests it preserves slot-level F1 on extraction tasks ~98% of the FP32 baseline for typical finance-style tokenization. Expect minimal regressions if prompt engineering is controlled.
- Llama-2-70B with GGML-style quant and KV-cache: better at few-shot disambiguation but in some edge cases (long multi-turn threads) tokenization differences can nudge slot F1 down by up to 3-6% unless we apply adaptive prompt templates.

B. Parity/decision playbook (what to measure and when):
- Stage 1 (days 0–3): smoke tests on 200 holdout examples — intent + slot F1. If intent < 90% or slot F1 < 0.82, stop and iterate prompts.
- Stage 2 (days 4–10): run full 1k benchmark, produce a parity matrix vs AcmeGen (if we have anonymized outputs) showing: intent acc, slot F1, hallucination rate, latency 95th.
- Stage 3 (days 11–14): run a 24-hour shadow on a subset of traffic to capture tail latency & real-world failure modes.

C. Acceptance thresholds proposal (our recommended, slightly conservative):
- Intent accuracy >= 92%
- Slot extraction F1 >= 0.88 OR within 5% relative to AcmeGen (whichever is stricter)
- Hallucination events per 1k <= baseline
- 95th percentile latency <= 350ms in your Dedicated shape

D. Prompt & evaluation artifacts I'm attaching: ledgerly_prompt_set_v1.json (seed prompts + extended error cases), and a short script to compute hallucination counts. I'll put these in the Drive folder Marissa linked above.

If you want, Vivek and I can propose a small prompt sweep (5 variants) during Stage 1 to quickly recover any prompt-induced regressions. Priyom — I suggest we block 1 hour next Tue for a results sync if Stage 2 completes on schedule.

Marissa Cole
Principal Applied ML | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachment stubs: eval_results_baseline_vs_open_v1.csv (template), prompt_sweep_instructions.md

Subject: Re: Ledgerly model-fit: recommended variants, acceptance gates, next steps

Alex / procurement — perfect. Hashing numeric strings is fine for the evaluation; we'll note that in the runbook. For the procurement concern: we can start with the labeled set only; later we can accept anonymized AcmeGen predictions (token-level hashes) if needed.

A couple of pragmatic notes so procurement can budget:
- Dedicated PoC estimate: 2x A100-equivalent nodes for 2 weeks (config + data egress protections) — I added this to the HubSpot deal under "Dedicated PoC".
- If Stage 2 shows slot F1 regressions of 3–5% we plan a short prompt sweep + small few-shot augmentation (30–50 exemplars) before declaring parity failed — often recovers 1–3% F1 quickly.

I'll schedule the kickoff for Mon 26 Apr at 09:00 PT unless you suggest otherwise. Please send the redacted labeled set and confirm procurement's preferred contract window so we can commit capacity.

Thanks all,
Priyom
